thread:
maya: Heads-up — Argus Bank wants a short POC for customer-managed keys (HSM) before signing. They need: CMK in their CloudHSM, attestations, a dry-run rotation, and a perf check at 99th p99 < 120ms on their 8k qps workload. Can we scope?
simon: Ack. Do we have an approved flow for BYO-CMK for Dedicated/private? I can sketch infra.
eli: Security Qs: they want FIPS 140-2 level 3 attestation, HSM vendor name + firmware signing proof, and key ceremony runbook. We'll need legal signoff on attestation delivery SLA.
nina: Pricing note — HSM add-on + attestation cost is usually a one-time plus monthly ops fee. I'll pull recent SOW numbers.
simon: For the POC infra I propose: staging VPC peered to customer, HSM proxy in their subnet (no key egress), Redwood runtime using external KMS plugin that talks to customer HSM over mTLS. Canary user traffic only.
maya: They also asked about rotation window: minimum downtime allowed is 10s, but they want a dry-run schedule to not impact live traffic. Any automations?
ops-eng: We have a rotation dry-run tool but it assumes our KMS. For BYO HSM we'd run a shadow rotation: create new KEK in HSM, push policy to runtime, warm caches, then flip. We can script that — estimated 2 engineers half-day to template.
eli: Add requirement: HSM must support import/export of wrapped keys (or a split-KEK approach). If not, we need proxy wrapping. Also request: key usage audit logs forwarded to their SIEM for 90 days.
maya: They sent a short security questionnaire excerpt. Key Q: "Can Redwood guarantee that CMKs never leave customer's HSM in plaintext?" — can we answer?
simon: Short answer: yes. Our runtime never exfiltrates plaintext keys; we use wrapped key material and in-HSM ops. I'll draft a one-liner and technical appendix.
nina: Pricing question from procurement: what is the incremental cost for HSM throughput for sustained 8k qps? They asked for an estimate they can budget.
ops-eng: Depends on GPU inference token throughput vs key ops. If each request requires a KEK unwrap per call it's expensive. Recommend ephemeral session keys cached per instance to amortize unwraps. Estimate: add-on ~$6k–12k/mo depending on scaling and HA. (very rough).
eli: Also flag: attestation lead time is vendor-dependent. If they require on-prem hardware attestation, add 3–6 weeks lead.
maya: Action items: @simon can you draft the tech appendix and sample runbook? @nina please pull 3 SOW examples + price ranges. @eli we'll need a one-pager security answer for the questionnaire. I'll coordinate with the customer to lock a POC start window (preferably 2 weeks out).
simon: Will do. Draft ETA EOD tomorrow.
nina: I'll post SOW snippets here by EOD and a conservative budget number.
eli: I'll draft security one-pager and send to legal. One question to legal: can we provide vendor firmware signing proof as part of attestation?
presales-bot: Reminder: create a POC workspace ticket and tag "sales-poc". Link: https://redwood.internal/tasks/POC-1737654321
maya: Thanks — also they're asking for a short test we can run that shows end-to-end latency with their HSM in the loop. Something reproducible.
simon: Proposed quick test (to run from customer's test VM):
```
curl -X POST https://redwood-staging.example/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <test-token>" 
  -d '{"prompt":"ping","max_tokens":1}'
```
This will exercise KEK unwrap on cold start; run a 5k sample and measure p99. We'll include script for parallel clients.
maya: Perfect. I'll send script to their infra lead. Anything else?
eli: One more: request they add a low-privilege service account for audit log forwarding. Saves time on compliance checks.
ops-eng: Noted. Also suggest we propose an SLA escape hatch: if perf can't meet p99 target we fallback to a Redwood-managed CMK variant (with customer's approval) for the POC. Need to get that option in writing now.
maya: Good call. I'll include fallback clause in the SOW draft. :thumbsup:
